description: Add the first-class Solana sBPF target front-end: a `sbf-solana-solana` triple that parses to { .bpfel, .solana, .solana }, the sbpfv1/sbpfv2/sbpfv3 CPU models with sbpfv3 as the solana default, dynamic-linkability for the solana target, routing through the self-hosted Elf2 linker (bypassing LLD), and a no-compiler_rt default. After this feature `sig targets` lists the new os/abi/cpu, `-target sbf-solana-solana` resolves correctly, and `sig build-lib -dynamic -target sbf-solana-solana` no longer dead-ends at TargetCannotDynamicLink or LLD's `unsupported e_machine value: 247`. Depends on FEAT-001 (confirms sbpfv3 is the version to default to). This is all target-table / option-resolution plumbing; the actual linker reloc work is FEAT-003.
steps: Read .agents/tasks/sbpf-solana/context.json and .agents/tasks/sbpf-solana/design.md §2-§5 FIRST; context.json replaces re-exploration.

In lib/std/Target.sig: add `solana` to Os.Tag and `solana` to the Abi enum. Add a `.solana` arm at every `.sb0` site mirroring freestanding-like behavior (verified lines 162, 403, 844, 2335, 2501, 2942, 3251), plus the Abi `.sb0` arms. OVERRIDE at line 1091: `.solana` keeps the normal ELF object format, NOT `.raw` (add it to the ELF/else branch). After editing, re-grep `\.sb0` and confirm every site has a matching `.solana` arm or a deliberate override.

In lib/std/Target.sig: add an `isSolana` predicate next to `isSb0` (~line 2251): true when os.tag == .solana and abi == .solana and (cpu.arch == .bpfel or .bpfeb). Add a default-CPU branch keyed on `os.tag == .solana => &bpf.cpu.sbpfv3` ahead of the existing `.bpfel, .bpfeb => &bpf.cpu.v3` default (~line 2120).

In lib/std/Target.sig triple parsing (the arch-name lookup used by std.Target.Query.parse): accept `sbf` as an input arch alias mapping to `.bpfel`, and `solana` as both os and abi, so `sbf-solana-solana` round-trips to the canonical { .bpfel, .solana, .solana } and displays back correctly (design-review NIT 1).

In lib/std/Target/bpf.sig under `pub const cpu`: add sbpfv1 (llvm_name "v1", no features), sbpfv2 (llvm_name "v2", no features), sbpfv3 (llvm_name "v3", features .alu32). Add a comment noting the manual addition so a future tools/update_cpu_features.sig regen preserves it. Add a synthetic `static_syscalls` Feature member and include it in sbpfv3 ONLY if FEAT-001's PC-SYS selected a codegen-visible toggle; otherwise omit it.

In src/target.sig: change canDynamicLink (~line 14) so `.bpfeb, .bpfel => target.os.tag == .solana` (generic bpfel-freestanding stays non-dynamic). Audit the `.bpfel/.bpfeb` PIE/stack-protector/red-zone arms and leave them BPF-wide (no behavior change for solana).

In src/Compilation/Config.sig: in the use_lld decision block (~line 410) force use_lld=false for os.tag == .solana (return an error if the user explicitly passed -fuse-lld, since sBPF needs the self-hosted linker). In the use_new_linker block (~line 461) force it true for os.tag == .solana.
In src/Compilation.sig (~line 1807): change the want_compiler_rt default to `const want = options.want_compiler_rt orelse (is_exe_or_dyn_lib and target.os.tag != .solana);`.

Add/extend unit tests (in lib/std/Target.sig and src/target.sig test blocks) asserting: sbf-solana-solana resolves to { .bpfel, .solana, .solana } with default -mcpu sbpfv3; canDynamicLink true for solana, false for bpfel-freestanding; want_compiler_rt default resolves false for solana.
Build with `sig build -Denable-llvm` and run `sig targets`. Commit on branch feat/sbpf-solana.
acceptance_criteria: `sig build -Denable-llvm` builds a compiler with these edits with no exhaustiveness errors.
The built `sig targets` lists the solana os/abi and the sbpfv1/sbpfv2/sbpfv3 CPU models.

A unit test asserts `-target sbf-solana-solana` resolves to { .bpfel, .solana, .solana } with default -mcpu sbpfv3, canDynamicLink is true for solana and false for bpfel-freestanding, and want_compiler_rt defaults false for solana.

`sig build-lib -dynamic -target sbf-solana-solana ...` no longer errors with TargetCannotDynamicLink nor with LLD `unsupported e_machine value: 247` (it now routes through Elf2; it may fail later for not-yet-implemented reloc support — that is FEAT-003).
re-grep of `\.sb0` in lib/std/Target.sig shows a matching `.solana` arm or deliberate override at every site.
verification: `sig build -Denable-llvm` from the worktree root exits 0.
Run the freshly built `sig targets` and confirm solana + sbpfv1/2/3 appear.
`sig build test` passes the target/dynamic-link/compiler_rt unit tests added here.
findings:
FEAT-002 target/option plumbing implemented and verified to the maximum the Windows host allows.

FILES CHANGED (6):
- lib/std/Target.sig: added Os.Tag.solana (after .sb0) and Abi.solana (after .sb0). Added a .solana arm at EVERY exhaustive os-tag switch that had a .sb0 arm, mirroring freestanding/.sb0 (no-libc, no-dynamic-loader, VersionRange .none): versionRangeTag, VersionRange.default, requiresLibC-style false group (~2360), DynamicLinker.kind .none group (~2527), DynamicLinker.standard no-path group (~2969), cTypeBitSize freestanding group (~3279). Abi.default: `.solana => .solana`. ObjectFormat.default OVERRIDE: `.solana => .elf` (NOT .raw like .sb0 — sBPF ships an ELF .so). Cpu.Model.baseline: `.bpfel/.bpfeb => switch(os.tag){ .solana => &bpf.cpu.sbpfv3, else => &bpf.cpu.v3 }` so solana defaults to sbpfv3. Added `pub inline fn isSolana` next to isSb0 (os==.solana and abi==.solana and arch in {.bpfel,.bpfeb}).
- lib/std/Target/Query.sig: `sbf` arch alias -> .bpfel in both parse() and parseCpuArch(). os/abi 'solana' round-trip via stringToEnum (no change needed). Added test cases asserting sbf-solana-solana -> {.bpfel,.solana,.solana}, ofmt=.elf, no dyn linker, isSolana, default cpu model name 'sbpfv3'; plus bare bpfel-solana -> abi .solana + sbpfv3.
- lib/std/Target/bpf.sig: added cpu.sbpfv1 (llvm_name v1, no feats), sbpfv2 (v2, no feats), sbpfv3 (v3, feats {.alu32}) with a MANUAL-ADDITION comment for update_cpu_features.sig regen. NO synthetic static_syscalls feature added: FEAT-001 PC-SYS confirmed static syscalls are a codegen `call imm` lowering (FEAT-004), not a codegen-visible LLVM feature toggle (this resolves FEAT-002 step 5's conditional).
- src/target.sig: canDynamicLink `.bpfeb,.bpfel => target.os.tag == .solana` (solana dynamic-linkable, generic bpfel-freestanding stays false). Other BPF-wide arms (PIE/red-zone/stack-protector at ~215/372/423/824) left unchanged. Added test block (testTarget helper + 2 tests) asserting canDynamicLink true for solana / false for bpfel-freestanding, and the want_compiler_rt default expression resolves false for solana / true for a generic dyn-lib target.
- src/Compilation/Config.sig: use_lld block forces false for os==.solana (returns error.LldIncompatibleObjectFormat if -fuse-lld was explicitly set); use_new_linker block forces true for os==.solana. Routes sBPF through the self-hosted Elf2 linker, bypassing LLD.
- src/Compilation.sig: want_compiler_rt default is now `options.want_compiler_rt orelse (is_exe_or_dyn_lib and target.os.tag != .solana)` so on-chain builds never pull in soft-float compiler_rt.

EXTRA EXHAUSTIVENESS SITES beyond the FEAT list (found by building; design said 'build until clean, do not trust the list alone'): lib/std/sig/llvm/Builder.sig llvm_os switch (.solana => "unknown", freestanding-like — Solana-ness is in linking, not the LLVM triple) and llvm_abi switch (.solana => "unknown"); lib/std/sig/LibCDirs.sig libCGenericName abi switch (.solana => unreachable, no libc); lib/std/start.sig native_os switch (.solana in the no-_start-export group — loader uses the `entrypoint` symbol). src/link.sig / src/link/Sb0.sig / src/codegen*.sig matches are link-tag/.cast dispatch or the separate compiler/core Target_Triple, NOT std.Target exhaustive switches, so no change needed; solana ofmt=.elf routes to the Elf2 link tag which FEAT-003 teaches to accept EM_BPF.

VERIFICATION:
- `sig build` (plain) compiles the whole compiler + stdlib clean (0 exhaustiveness errors) and the `test` step (compiler/test_all.sig) passes exit 0.
- Freshly built `sig targets` lists `solana` in BOTH the os list and the abi list, and sbpfv1/sbpfv2 (no features) + sbpfv3 (alu32) under bpfel and bpfeb.
- `sig-out/bin/sig.exe build-lib -dynamic -target sbf-solana-solana -mcpu sbpfv3 entry.sig` NO LONGER errors TargetCannotDynamicLink nor LLD 'unsupported e_machine value: 247'. It now reaches codegen and fails with 'producing machine code via LLVM requires using the LLVM library' — expected, because this sig.exe was built WITHOUT -Denable-llvm; proves target resolution + dynamic-link + linker routing all pass. The remaining reloc work is FEAT-003.
- New test bodies in Query.sig + Target.sig semantically analyze clean via `sig test lib/std/std.sig -fno-emit-bin --test-no-exec` (exit 0).

KNOWN ENV BLOCKERS (pre-existing, NOT caused by FEAT-002, flagged for later features):
1. `sig build -Denable-llvm` fails in ~4s with 'dependency cycle detected: cycle detected among unvisited nodes' from the stage0 build runner, BEFORE any source compiles. build.sig has ZERO diff vs base branch (fix/resinator-sig-lib-dir-and-win32-resource), so this is a pre-existing build-graph bug in the LLVM pipeline wiring on this host, independent of these edits. FEAT-003/004 need an LLVM-enabled compiler to emit/link real BPF — this build-graph cycle must be resolved (or built on Linux/WSL) before those features can run their full codegen verification on Windows.
2. Executing the full stdlib test binary on this Windows host fails at LINK time with a malformed vendored compiler_rt.lib ('invalid value 608 for weak external symbol'); -fno-compiler-rt then leaves soft-float symbols (__floatunsitf, __trunctfdf2, roundf128, ...) undefined from unrelated zon/json float code. So the std unit tests can be compile-checked but not executed as a linked binary here. The canonical compiler/test_all.sig suite DOES run and passes.

FOR FEAT-003 (linker): solana target now has ofmt=.elf, use_lld=false, use_new_linker=true, so compilation flows into src/link/Elf2.sig. Elf2's EhdrMachine enum still lacks BPF (247) and will panic at the 'add support for target machine' seam until FEAT-003 adds it. Reloc values to implement (from FEAT-001 PC2): R_SBF_64_64=1, R_SBF_64_ABS64=2, R_SBF_64_32=10; REL form (SHT_REL, implicit addends); lddw split low32->slot1 imm, high32->slot2 imm; targetPageAlign for BPF = 0x8 (per PC3, NOT 0x1000). Final deploy artifact is static/relocation-free ET_DYN with only .rodata/.text/.shstrtab (PC3).
